title: The :3001 API's root doc blob advertises 18 available contracts while the endpoint serves 57, and CORS is open to every origin
description: `GET /` returns a static documentation blob listing a hand-written `availableContracts` array of 18 names; `GET /contracts` actually serves 57. Both loaders are hard-wired to chainId 31337 and the response shape does not match the `{networks:{...}, activeNetwork, availableNetworks}` contract documented in the project CLAUDE.md. `cors()` is applied with no origin allowlist.
impact: A UI developer integrating against the documented surface sees a third of what exists. Local-only and low consequence — anvil binds loopback here, though `npm run start:anvil` uses `--host 0.0.0.0`, which binds every interface.
attackPath: No protocol attack path. GET / returns a static blob listing a hand-written availableContracts array of 18 names while GET /contracts serves 57; both loaders are hard-wired to chainId 31337 and the response shape does not match the {networks, activeNetwork, availableNetworks} contract documented in the project CLAUDE.md; cors() is applied with no origin allowlist.
evidence: Live run: `curl localhost:3001/` -> availableContracts length 18; `curl localhost:3001/contracts` -> 57 keys. Health endpoint confirms deploymentsLoaded/extractedAddressesLoaded true, chainId 31337.
recommendation: Derive the root blob's contract list from local.json rather than hand-maintaining it, or drop the list and point at /contracts. Reconcile the response shape with CLAUDE.md, or update CLAUDE.md to describe what is actually served.

classification.c4Criterion: C4 QA - stale documentation / drift. The second half is developer-workstation hygiene, not a protocol issue.
classification.assetImpact: None. No protocol asset is reachable: the chain is anvil 31337 and every token on it is a mock.
attackPath: No protocol attack path. GET / returns a static blob listing a hand-written availableContracts array of 18 names while GET /contracts serves 57; both loaders are hard-wired to chainId 31337 and the response shape does not match the {networks, activeNetwork, availableNetworks} contract documented in the project CLAUDE.md; cors() is applied with no origin allowlist.
classification.likelihood: Certain but inconsequential (verified live: root blob length 18, /contracts 57 keys).
classification.externalRequirements: For the exposure half: an untrusted party on the same LAN while `npm run start:anvil` is running with --host 0.0.0.0.

severityRationale: QA, matching the auditor's proposal. Splitting the rationale deliberately, because the deduplicator flagged that a themed 'stale docs' heading could bury the second half. HALF ONE - the 18-vs-57 doc blob and the CLAUDE.md shape mismatch - is low-value drift: a UI developer integrating against the documented surface sees a third of what exists. Pure QA. HALF TWO - `cors()` with no allowlist combined with `npm run start:anvil --host 0.0.0.0`, on a chain that per DEV-05 has unlimited mock minting and an unrevoked phUSD minter grant to the deployer - is the load-bearing part and is retained explicitly so it is not lost. It still does not exceed QA: the assets reachable are mocks on a throwaway chain, CORS governs browser fetches and does not gate the RPC at all, and the meaningful exposure is the 0.0.0.0 anvil binding rather than anything in server/index.js. Correctly framed, that is developer-workstation hygiene - bind loopback unless a LAN device genuinely needs access - not a protocol finding, and inflating it would be exactly the overstatement this pipeline rejects.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
